detections.summary: Hosts discuss extensive sleep hygiene practices covering room temperature, light, noise, timing, caffeine, alcohol, exercise, screens, naps, bedding, diet, and anxiety-driven insomnia techniques.

detections.evidence_quote: As a board certified sleep physician, I have seen this pattern in my own patients over and over again in the clinic
detections.summary: Host invokes being a board-certified sleep physician and clinical experience with patients as grounds for the following generalization.
Host attributes the effectiveness of consistency in sleep habits to personal experience.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Keeping the bedroom around sixty-five degrees Fahrenheit helps most people sleep better.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: most folks sleep better somewhere around sixty five degrees
verification_candidates.rationale: Specific temperature claim for sleep quality that could be checked against sleep research.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Even small amounts of light from a hallway or streetlight can disrupt deeper stages of sleep.

verification_candidates.rationale: Checkable claim about ambient light disrupting deep sleep stages.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Alcohol fragments sleep later in the night.

verification_candidates.claim_text: Exercising earlier in the day tends to help sleep quality.
verification_candidates.evidence_quote: Exercise earlier in the day tends to help sleep quality
verification_candidates.rationale: Checkable claim about exercise timing and sleep quality.
